Alder read it twice, then climbed the tower and read it aloud to the lamp, because someone ought to hear it, and because the light carried further than he could.", "w02": "凌晨四点，城市像一个尚未醒透的人。路灯还亮着，橘黄的光摊在空无一人的柏油路上，被洒水车碾出一道湿痕。早点铺的卷帘门哗啦升起，蒸笼冒出第一口白气，面团在案板上被摔得沉闷。环卫工的扫帚沿着路牙来回，声音干燥而耐心。写字楼只剩零星几格窗亮着，像没拔掉的插头。地铁尚未启动，站口的铁栅栏锁着昨夜的风。远处高架上偶有一辆货车掠过，轰鸣像从梦里经过。天边开始泛出极薄的灰蓝，一切都在等那一声鸟叫。", "w03": "- Recursion is when something solves a problem by asking a smaller copy of itself to do the same job.\n- Imagine standing in a long line and wanting to know your position: you ask the person ahead, \"What number are you?\" and add one — and the very first person just says \"I'm number one\" without asking anyone.\n- That last step is the important part: every recursion needs a stopping point, or the questions would go on forever."}
